steps.text: Craft a **Chassis** (iron + copper) and a few **Blank Module Plates** (iron + copper).

steps: Craft a **Fuel Engine** (blank + furnace + copper), a **Heater** (blank + furnace) and an **Inventory Access Panel** (blank + barrel).

steps.text: Place the chassis. Hold each module and use it on a side: engine on the bottom, heater on top, panel on the front.
Right-click the panel with an empty hand. Put raw iron in **Orange** storage and coal in **Purple** storage.

steps: Iron ingots appear in **Green** storage. Take them out through the panel. That's it: no settings needed.

pages.text: A step **turns green with a tick** once you have done it in your world.

**Three storages, three jobs.** Every machine has an Orange, a Green and a Purple storage (and a tank of each colour). Modules start out the same way: they **take from Orange**, put **results into Green**, and take **fuel and tools from Purple**. So most machines work as soon as you put the modules on.

Each module's side has a thin **coloured ring** near its edge showing which storages it uses, in the same colours (a paler shade for tanks). A module that uses two gets a ring in two sections, like a heater: orange (takes from) and green (results go to).
The finished layout. Click a side to read about its module.
**Try it here first.** This bench simulates the same machine with no world involved. Press play and watch the RF graph rise and fall as the heater works.

**Why did it stop?** Right-click the chassis with an empty hand to open the **machine screen**, then click the side. It says what the module is doing and, if something is wrong, what to do about it, for example *Green storage is full. Take things out of Green storage.* See [[fieldframe:basics/configurator|the machine screen]].
